title: Beti or Bati bar Tuvia
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Kiddushin 70b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.70b.10): Rav Yehuda proclaimed that Beti bar Tuvia, because of his haughtiness, did not take the bill of freedom. And [at the end of Avodah Zarah (76b)](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.76b.3-4) it is told that Mar Yehuda (and the reading of Rashi and Tosafot is Rav Yehuda) and Bati bar Tuvi were sitting before King Shapur, and an etrog was brought before them. King Shapur cut off a piece and ate it; he cut off a piece and gave it to Bati bar Tuvi; he then stabbed (the knife) ten times into the ground and gave it to Mar Yehuda. Bati said to him: And am I not a son of Israel? He said to him: Remember what you did in the evening. (And [Rashi explains](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Avodah_Zarah.76b.4.1): it was the custom of the Persians to hand over women to guests; Rav Yehuda did not accept them, but Bati accepted them. And [Tosafot there explain](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Avodah_Zarah.76b.4.1) that he did not sin in this, since he was still partly a slave, his bill of release being withheld.)[^1][^2]

notes.text: Beti/Bati, Tuvia/Tuvi and Mar/Rav Yehudah remain reported variants. The knife is thrust into the ground ten times; the source’s explanation about the women and his partly enslaved status remains the commentators’ argument.

The linked Avodah Zarah has Mar Yehudah and Bati bar Tuvi. It presents the rebuke about the previous evening as an alternative response. Rashi and Tosafot give Rav Yehudah. Tosafot’s explanation turns on Bati still lacking his release document.
